title: revenexx metrics.json (v1)
description: The semantic layer of a revenexx app or Cube: the business numbers it defines and the dimensions they can be cut by. A metric is declared, never written as SQL — an aggregation (sum, count, average, …) over a view or dataset from the analytics.json next to this file, optionally over a restricted column expression and narrowed by structured filters, or a formula over other metrics. The platform compiles every metric into the query itself, so the same definition of "net revenue" drives a KPI tile, a chart, a report table, an export and an answer from the AI assistant, and nobody re-derives it in a spreadsheet. Dimensions name the columns worth grouping by and how they join across apps (a shared day, market or campaign), which is what lets a Cube put its ad spend next to an app's revenue. Money is always reported per currency and never converted.

$schema.description: Reference to this JSON Schema for editor validation and autocompletion.

dimensions.description: The columns metrics can be grouped, filtered and joined by. Keys are unique within the file; another app or Cube refers to one as "<app>.<dimension>".

metrics.description: The numbers this app or Cube defines. Keys are unique within the file; another app, Cube, report or dashboard refers to one as "<app>.<metric>".

localizableText.description: Operator-facing text. Either a plain string — which the Cockpit shows in every UI language — or a map of BCP-47 language tag to text. 'en' is required and is what the Cockpit falls back to when its UI locale has no entry, so a half-translated file degrades to English rather than to a blank label. Every entry must hold at least one non-blank character.

dimension.description: A column worth grouping by, from exactly one view or dataset.

key.description: Dimension key, unique within the file (e.g. "day", "market", "status").

label.description: Label shown in pickers, axis titles and table headers.

view.description: Name of a view in this package's analytics.json. Exactly one of `view` or `dataset`.

dataset.description: Name of a dataset in this package's analytics.json. Exactly one of `view` or `dataset`.

column.description: The column of that view or dataset.

vocabulary.description: Labels for coded values, as a map of stored value → label (e.g. "cancelled" → "Cancelled"). Values without an entry are shown as stored.

lookup.description: A view whose rows label the values of this column, as "<app>.<view>" — e.g. a market id shown by the market's name from "markets.markets". The column is matched against that view's key, and the view's first text column is the label.

grain.description: For a time column: the finest grain it is meaningful at. Coarser grains (week, month, quarter, year) are derived by the platform; finer ones are refused. A date column is at most 'day'.

joins.description: The conformed dimension this one is the same thing as, as "<app>.<dimension>" (e.g. "orders.day", "markets.market", "campaigns.campaign"). Declaring it is what lets a report put metrics from two apps or Cubes side by side on one axis: rows meet where both sides hold the same value. Without it, metrics from different packages can still share a report, but not a breakdown.

metric.description: One business number. Either a base metric — `agg` over a view or dataset — or a derived metric — a `derived` formula over other metrics. Never both.

oneOf.title: A base metric aggregates a view or dataset
A derived metric is a formula over other metrics

key.description: Metric key, unique within the file (e.g. "revenue_net").

label.description: Name of the metric on tiles, legends and table headers.

description.description: What the metric means and how it is counted, shown in the metric catalog and as a tooltip. Say what is excluded — "net of discounts, without cancelled orders" saves a support ticket.

hint.description: A short caption shown under the KPI value (e.g. "excl. cancelled").

view.description: Base metric: the view in this package's analytics.json it aggregates. Exactly one of `view` or `dataset`.

dataset.description: Base metric: the dataset in this package's analytics.json it aggregates. Exactly one of `view` or `dataset`.

agg.description: Base metric: the aggregation. 'count' without `expr` counts rows; 'count_distinct' counts distinct values of `expr` (e.g. contact_id for buyers).

expr.description: Base metric: what is aggregated — a column, or arithmetic over columns and numbers of the same view or dataset (e.g. "subtotal - discount_total"). Only column names, numbers, + - * /, parentheses and spaces: no functions, no quotes, no SQL. Omitted with 'count', rows are counted.

filters.description: Base metric: rows that count, as structured conditions that must all hold (e.g. status is not cancelled). Structured rather than a WHERE string, so a filter can be shown to the reader and cannot inject anything.

time.description: Base metric: the column that places a row in time for period scoping and trends. Defaults to the view's or dataset's `roles.time`.

derived.description: Derived metric: a formula over metric keys and numbers (e.g. "revenue_net / orders_count"). A key may be qualified as "<app-or-cube>.<metric>" to use another package's metric ("orders.revenue_net / ad_cost"); the other package must be installed for the metric to resolve. Same restricted grammar as `expr`: + - * /, parentheses and spaces, no functions. Write a minus with spaces around it after a qualified key, since a package name may itself contain hyphens. Division by zero yields no value, not an error.

format.description: How the value is shown. 'money' — an amount, reported per currency (see `currency`); 'count' — a whole number of things; 'number' — any other number; 'percent' — a ratio shown as a percentage (0.25 → 25 %); 'ratio' — a plain ratio (ROAS 3.2); 'duration' — seconds, shown as a duration.

currency.description: For a money metric: the column holding the ISO 4217 currency code. The metric is then computed and reported per currency, never converted — a tenant selling in EUR and CHF sees two numbers, not an invented sum.

direction.description: Whether a rising value is good news. Colors the change against the comparison period: 'up_is_good' (revenue) shows a rise in green, 'down_is_good' (return rate, cost per order) in red. Omitted, changes are shown neutral.

filter.description: One condition on a column. 'in' and 'not_in' take a list, 'is_null' and 'not_null' take no value, every other operator takes one value.

column.description: The column the condition is on.

value.description: The value compared against: a string, number or boolean, or a list of them for 'in' and 'not_in'.
